blindSummary:
Trans visitors face serious risk here. Two penal-code provisions criminalise same-sex conduct (up to 14 years) with documented recent enforcement: an international human-rights organisation's November 2024 campaign highlights a 36-year-old health professional serving a 15-year sentence with hard labour simply for identifying as gay, and the same organisation's 2024 regional report documents rising hostility in this country. There is no legal gender recognition, religious leaders lead anti-LGBT mobilisation, and police are perpetrators more than protectors.

For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest; the documented serving-sentence case shows courts impose maximum terms.
blindOutOfScope: Same-sex criminalisation is the vehicle; trans people are captured via birth-sex status and indecency provisions.
blindSourceSummaries: International human-rights organisation campaign story (Nov 2024): profile of a 36-year-old health professional serving a 15-year prison sentence with hard labour simply for identifying as gay - a portrait of his medical career, service during the pandemic, and imprisonment.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust's country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to 14 years).

International human-rights organisation report (Jan 2024), its title conveying that the community is facing extinction: escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment and the weaponisation of law and their human-rights implications across several countries on the continent - country profiles including this country, documenting the 2022/23 surge in fear, attacks, oppression and hostility.

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under two penal-code provisions; societal discrimination; arrests and prosecutions reported.

International human-rights organisation report (July 2016) on debased dignity: forced anal examinations in homosexuality prosecutions - reported in at least eight countries in five years; lack evidentiary value and constitute cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment that may amount to torture; victims described them as painful, degrading, and a form of sexual violence (this country among those documented).
A foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - continued criminalisation and societal discrimination.
A foreign government's 2010 human-rights report on this country (archived): documents criminalisation and societal discrimination - baseline assessment.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 14 years, active enforcement) — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
